Class RunnerJarURLConnection

java.lang.Object
java.net.URLConnection
java.net.JarURLConnection
io.micronaut.runner.protocol.jar.RunnerJarURLConnection
public final class RunnerJarURLConnection extends JarURLConnection
A connection to an entry of a runner archive, served from the index and the memory mapped archive.

One identity, consistently

JarURLConnection splits a URL at the first "!/", so for the nested form jar:file:/app.jar!/MICRONAUT-INF/lib/dep.jar!/a/B.class it would call the entry MICRONAUT-INF/lib/dep.jar!/a/B.class — a name no jar has and no JarFile would find. A library that asks the same connection for the jar, the entry name and the entry would get three answers that do not describe the same thing. This class overrides every one of them so that they agree. For the URL above:

  • getJarFileURL() is jar:file:/app.jar!/MICRONAUT-INF/lib/dep.jar
  • getEntryName() is a/B.class
  • getJarFile() is the NestedJarFile of that dependency
  • getJarEntry() is that jar's entry a/B.class

For an entry of the application layer, jar:file:/app.jar!/MICRONAUT-INF/classes/a/B.class, the answers are the ordinary ones over the outer archive: the jar URL is file:/app.jar, the entry name is MICRONAUT-INF/classes/a/B.class, and the jar is the outer archive as an ordinary JarFile. The entry itself comes from the index record the connection resolved rather than from that JarFile, because the application layer's directories are recorded in the index and are not entries of the outer archive: asking the archive for one would answer null for a URL whose getEntryName() is not null and whose getInputStream() works, and the four answers would stop describing the same thing.

A URL that names a whole nested jar, whether it ends with "!/" or stops at the jar, streams the bytes of that jar, so that code which wants to treat a dependency as an archive can.

Where the bytes come from

An entry the index knows is streamed straight out of the archive, with no java.util.zip machinery and no temporary file. Only the outer archive's own entries, the launcher classes, the manifest and the index itself, fall back to a real JarFile of the outer archive, opened once and on demand. Every call to getInputStream() returns a fresh stream, whatever setUseCaches was told, because micronaut-core reads service files by disabling caches and then asking for the stream, and because there is no shared state here that a second read could disturb.

    • getJarEntry

      public JarEntry getJarEntry() throws IOException
      The entry this connection reads.

      For a versioned entry of the application layer the outer archive holds the bytes under the META-INF/versions/<n>/ name, so that is the entry reported, in the same spirit as JarEntry.getRealName().

      An application layer entry is described from the index record, which is where its size, checksum, compression method and timestamp are recorded and where getInputStream() already reads from. That is also the only way a directory of the application layer can be described at all: the layer is stored exploded and the outer archive carries no entry for every directory in it, so delegating to the outer JarFile would answer null for a URL that resolves perfectly well, and conn.getJarEntry().isDirectory() - the usual way to classify a class path URL - would fail with a NullPointerException.

      Overrides:
      getJarEntry in class JarURLConnection
      Returns:
      the entry, or null when the URL names a whole jar
      Throws:
      IOException - if the jar cannot be opened

    • setUseCaches

      public void setUseCaches(boolean useCaches)
      Records the caching preference without the IllegalStateException the super class throws after a connection is connected.

      Nothing here caches anything a caller could observe: streams are opened fresh from the archive every time, so the flag cannot make a read fail and a library that flips it late, as several do right before reading a service file, is simply obliged.

      Overrides:
      setUseCaches in class URLConnection
      Parameters:
      useCaches - whether caches may be used
